key_insight: Language models handle many materials calculations and physical explanations well but struggle with fine-grained response estimates, similar-state comparisons and quantitatively supported decisions.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-assisted materials discovery requires condition-aware reasoning and stable prediction updates as experimental evidence accumulates.
method: M1: Test unaided, condition-specific reasoning on 200 tasks across ten research functions using aluminium and high-entropy alloys.
M2: Evaluate agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions.
MatEvoBench-20: Evaluate initial forecasts and revisions of hidden responses across scientific dependency chains.
evidence_signal: Across eleven model deployments, related literature improved selected estimates, while progressive observations calibrated some downstream responses but destabilized some previously accurate predictions.
watch_item: Condition and baseline mismatches can limit knowledge transfer, so additional literature or observations should not be assumed to improve prediction reliability.
paper_title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
